notes.title: PSA on updates and the public beta branch
notes.content:
Hi everyone.

About updating

As you hopefully can tell, I'm very active here and on the discord trying to help everyone, listening to improvements and fixes that need to get done. And I'd make patches every day if I could . (I do, but more on that later)

And two updates have already been released. But I recently notices a few bug reports where folks were using a version with issues that had already been fixed..

So the main problem here is, that if you open steam and within lets say 20 seconds open bulwark, Steam does not get the time to quietly update the game, and you are missing the patches , and you won't even realize it.  

An example : some folks for a while had that issue where you only got the millwright commander that buffs wood extractors and provides a wood extractor. I re balanced that event as  I saw all the requests on where to get more extractors (conquest, alignment  and random encounters).

I made a mistake and for many hours folks reported that all random encounters where the wood lady.
Yet that bug was reported and fixed within 10 minutes (I was tired and did a last minute change after QA, won't happen again). But most importantly not everybody got that fix.  This is not ideal. 

So here are 4 ways to make sure you are up to date. 

[olist]
 Wait a minute before playing and often steam will start updating .
 In properties verify the local files, often this will force an update, but takes a long time
 Hard restart steam, close steam completely (not minimize, but force close) and it will update when you open it again after a few seconds.
 My favorite: go to properties /betas and select the beta patch from the beta list.  Then after it updates deselect it and it will update back to the normal version with all the updates.
[/olist]

Did you say beta patch?
Yes there is a beta patch you can turn on in properties/betas. It will give you my rapidly updating beta patch.  These are untested features and fixes , so do this and you might find new bugs. If you do report them in the discord or forums, because that is super useful. 

so for instance stuff that is in the current beta patch but hasn't passed Wired Productions QA is : 

 when you save during a loss of surveyor , you will get a new one at load
 when you try to assign captains during a loss of surveyor the menu won't lock
 the pause menu has buttons to go to the soultree screen
 the pause menu has buttons to go to the inventory screen (so many buttons)
 fixed the menu overlap on max UI scale


And I'm working on some late game issues with the wonders not unlocking after combat and a free unit exploit, players found.  So I literally add those fixes to the beta patch the moment they are done. 

I literally love fixing bugs,  it is the most satisfying thing in the world, and if someone reports something be sure that I will try to figure out what happened. 

And I really want everyone to be up to date on the latest QA certified patch or even the beta patch.

So enjoy and don't forget to update,
Tomas

notes.title: Bulwark Settlements Trailer
notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42854035/03376befe482892090deb6758b4c305a3827d37d.png

Hello residents of The Great Ursee!
We hope you've been enjoying your time with the Demo lately and the most recent updates for polish and balancing that went out over the weekend - today we want to share a little more information with you about what's to come, drop a brand new trailer, and say thank you for those that came to join us at WASD.

Breaking The Cycle

As well as the incoming updates, we're celebrating the introduction of these new landmarks with a brand new trailer that shows off some locations that will be familiar to long time fans of The Falconeer universe, and some of the sprawling settlements within the world - all made in game!

It's a bit of an epic compared to some of our pure gameplay trailers, and really helps set the scale and tone of Bulwark, so please give it a watch and share it far and wide with anyone that has even passively looked at a lego brick in their lives!

[previewyoutube=wZT_uTx9auU;full][/previewyoutube]

Speaking of The Falconeer, some of you may already be familiar with the architecture, landmarks and factions of The Great Ursee - though by the time Bulwark begins, the very nature of their existence in the world has changed quite drastically following the cataclysmic events at the end of The Falconeer.

In the upcoming weeks we'll take a look at each of the factions, share their past and impact on 'The Path' and what their motivations and state is as we move into Bulwark - which should serve as a nice refresher for those that have already soured the Ursee skies, and a bit of an education into the deep lore of the game for new players to the series - if you have any burning questions you wanted answered - let us know in the comments! 

Is That A Dreadnot In Your Pocket?

Those with sharp eyes will have spotted that the end of the trailer reveals a brand new unit that will be added to the game on launch as a 'thank you' to those who have wishlisted and picked up the game during the launch window! 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42854035/1f7c22e821f7ccb03b7fca2bc59a8b3fab374d37.png

The Pocket Dreadnot is a mighty naval unit with destructive power to spare should your attempts at diplomacy take a turn for the worst (or if you just want to flex that naval might to your neighbouring settlements!) 

We'll be sharing more information on the new commander and some footage of this unit in a future blog where we take a look at each of the benefits provided by captains and commanders you can discover in the world - so keep your eyes on these blogs, and be sure to wishlist and hit follow so you can get the updates as they come out as well as Tomas's frequent patch updates!

https://store.steampowered.com/app/290100/Bulwark_Falconeer_Chronicles/

The Settlements Update and Faction Interactions

Last week Tomas shared a blog with you detailing the addition of settlements to the game, and explaining some of the ways you can interact with them ( If you missed it, the previous blog -  can be found here).

As with all things initially added to the demo this is a super early first iteration of a brand new feature that adds an extra layer of mechanical depth and new way to interact with the inhabitants of the Great Ursee, helping to bring more choice and consequence to the decisions you make and attempting to give you agency over how conflicts start and play out as you spread your influence over the world.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42854035/2d7261fcdaa867fe225f3bdcd89f689cd2e0efa6.jpg

We've already had some great feedback regarding the addition of this lite diplomacy, both on a conceptual level and of course, the initial bugs that have been discovered in this early form. We're aiming to provide a couple more updates very shortly that should alleviate some of the rough edges around the settlements and how you interact with them based on your feedback - but as always, keep playing and let us know if anything feels off or wonky - this is a very new and exciting addition to Bulwark and we can't wait to see where it ends up, but your feedback is vital in helping shape it!

If you don't have time to play (we get it, life happens) Tomas has a couple of 'early test' videos up on his Youtube channel which you can view here in his dev diaries :

[previewyoutube=zIDDk3EoCjo;full][/previewyoutube]

[previewyoutube=I-8N7U_HgG0;full][/previewyoutube]


A Post WASD World

Finally, It's been a week since we brought the Ursee to London and got to watch a whole new host of builders and creators get their hands on Bulwark and begin crafting their legacies within The Ursee - we also were fortunate to catch a couple of interviews whilst we were there, sharing some discussion about  Bulwark, The Falconeer, Tomas, and yes - the burning question - Unity.

[previewyoutube=S8WqYUDVVHo;full][/previewyoutube]

If you managed to make it over to WASD and spend time with us, thank you - we hope we were able to be a small part of a great weekend for you, if you were unable to make the trip then fear not! We're going to leave the Evolving Demo up for a while whilst we gather more feedback and testing on the settlements and diplomacy features.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42854035/2a4a8d186ddfb8e3c081996e0e728dc649d9494a.jpg

What's next?

Phew, that was a pretty sizable update! But then again, between Gamescom, WASD, New updates and more, it has been a super busy couple of months so what lies on the horizon?


 We'll be sharing some previews and interviews with you all very soon.
 We'll be continuing to refine and update the settlements and diplomacy.
 We'll be sharing some more about the factions, world, lore and units within with you.
 If you're eager for more physical event presences - stay tuned, the year isn't over yet and we may very well be turning up at an event near you soon with some pretty exciting news to announce...


In the meantime, continue to play, to give us feedback, and please share your streams, screenshots, creations and opinions with us on socials and Discord - we love to see what you all make and share them with the world!

And as always, every wishlist and bit of hype around these announcement helps Tomas continue to do what he does best so get that trailer out there, hit that wishlist - and keep an eye on all your socials of choice below to get excited with us as he continues to Build that Bulwark!

notes.title: Evolving beyond the demo
notes.content:
Hi everyone,

Today a post about the future of Bulwark:

As you may have noticed the updates to the evolving demo have sort of trickled to a stop.  This is partially natural as many issues get addressed and new options added, but I’ve also found that it’s hard for me to focus on core development when there is so much demand for changes to controls or on-boarding.  

And it’s time to get some core development done. 

I want to get into the world more, develop the interactions with other factions, have proper conflict, perhaps even some naval strategy.There is also a ton of just production work I need to get done, the missing buildings and faction commanders and so forth. Basically all the good things myself and many players are dreaming of for the game. 

I also need a holiday badly, this year has been quite tumultuous in unpleasant ways.  So to get to the point:

After the Tiny Teams steam event august 10th , the evolving demo will be turned off and the game will go dark again.   

I am quite confident in saying that the evolving demo has brought massive changes and sometimes you all have had to be quite vocal to get your points across, but I hope and feel that the game is now so much better because of it.  There are multiple control templates and options to make the game feel more accessible and there has been 6 months of iteration to get it to where it is today.  And for that I am super grateful and want to thank everyone that posted here and on the discord with feedback.  

Thank you!

So will there never be access to the demo?  Of course not, there will be plenty of moments where the demo will be back, either as part of an event or just a quick test with the players off a new feature. But it won’t be there consistently. 

I will also return to handing out more full keys for closed testing via the Discord when new features get delivered, so if you want in , head to :
https://discord.com/invite/falconeer

So I fully expect to keep everyone updated here as to the progress and expect to be playing more advanced versions of the game here regularly.  

But first a holiday! 

Tomas

notes.title: Experimental camera panning on WASD now live (I did listen)
notes.content:
I have heard the chorus of people that dislike being stuck to a single tower in build mode. 
I even suspect many don't even make it to the surveyor flying mode that is meant to alleviate that. 

But I have been trying all kinds of prototypes for a long time to get something working that works with the tower focused building system.  That still allows for WASD camera motion across the screen. 

I think I've found something,

 it's not 100% perhaps what people expect, the camera is still tethered to the tower or surveyor, but the tether is now loose for a about a single screen (so you cannot pan and leave your selected tower, or surveyor out of view)

How it works:

-panning with WASD is now default, it's undocumented and experimental
-orbit now only on the MMB
- you cannot orbit and pan at the same time
-when you scroll down or zoom in, the pan resets itself to focus on your selected tower.
-panning is not supported on controller (tho I doubt controller users will miss it)

So two strong requests:

if you support this change, please please let me know in the comments, it's certainly a devation of the design vision and I need strong backup from everyone that had issues that yes this is going to alleviate your concerns.  This has been strangely, and I guess hard to understand, a very hard mechanic to get to work. It also does mess up the building of balconies, cuz that's now very hard when you are panned away.  But perhaps that's just the price of accesibility.

If you do not support this change, please please also let me know. 

I will make this option available permanent, but if this panning is turned on or off by default is up to you!

Anyways it's live now.. 
It might cause a lot of bugs, I haven't been able to test it properly. But would like the nextfest players to experience this.

Let me know what's broken please..


to those new, this might feel like a minor update, but both technically, conceptually and in the forum history I think this is the nr1 topic around the game.  so chime in please.

notes.title: Now live Update includes auto wall/walkway building and MMB mouse orbit and mor
notes.content:
Auto walkway/wall building when you spawn a basic tower on the ground
So I think one confusing aspect as reported is that you build a single tower on the ground and then what?
So I've added (this was suggested multiple times) an auto walkway that gets build when you build a tower.  This is quite an experimental bit of code, so there might be strangeness. hence it's being tested out on Discord first.


Secondly mouse orbit on MMB
Much has been said on what gets mapped to the WASD , in the end Bulwark is a game where you orbit the camera a lot.  The camera is always fixed to a tower or your surveyor (later fleet of units). 
But you can orbit/look around with the WASD.  This I agree is unconventional.  

One suggestion has been to add a regular MMB orbit mechanic, so WASD becomes a moot point as you won't ever have to use it (unless you prefer it).  Hopefully saving some confusion and frustration.

The orbit on MMB cannot work in conjunction with edge scrolling, so I've renamed that mouse camera turning in the controller settings. and you can set it to orbit now. (it is the default for new users, so I can see if it helps).

For those wanting a free camera, once you see how the new tower/walkway construction works you will notice it's a different mechanic and quite fun in its own right. Fixing the camera to the tower there makes total sense I hope.  And because I want the same mechanics in the air as on the ground, that means another reason why there cannot be a free camera when flying around. 

Just to reiterate there is no limited map , it's 10 km square open world you need to explore. So edge scrolling or just flying through that would not be as great as say in a more conventional builder or colony sim.  

Added some fun things

added mouse orbit on MMB not the default (kept that to edge scrolling) change it in the controller screen
added auto connect, walkways  on new towers are automatically built and connected.
fixed some things in the imperial outpost/citadel
fixed some collision issue with the freehouse big platform foundations
changed some texts
As a nice parting gif, you can now set your faction color in the setting, vehicle trim and flags will be set to it.


Enjoy  and reboot steam to force the update!

notes.title: The Builderfest demo is live!
notes.content:
Hi everyone,

As you can see the demo is now available. this is an unlimited version of the pre-alpha version. You can play thru the tutorial and beyond as random encounters are spawned after the tutorial. You can fly anywhere in the open world,. tho the area beyond the tutorial zone isn't filled up with content yet. You can still try to establish colonies in all the cool places of the Ursee. 

The demo also has a freebuild mode, which is a mode in which there are no constraints and you can build regardless of resources, a sort of experimental freeform mode.  It has little guidance and the tutorial is a good place to start, but if you feel that itch to explore and experiment without guidance, freebuild is the mode for you!


Updates
I actually put the demo online Sunday and have been working on an update based on the first feedback. That updated version is now available(monday). 

Most notably it improves control settings for mouse with separate axis for edge turning and inversion. It also explains better that the Surveyor isn't a direct control vehicle, it will fly towards your cursor location when you command it to.  But you do not steer it directly.  I added a little beacon to make this more intuitive. 

good examples of feedback being digested and turned into an update ;) Which is exactly the point of this demo. 

As you might know or not, this is a mostly solo developed game, so for me this is going to be an overwhelming week, but I am trying to respond to everyone personally.  If you have an issue or feedback please provide as much information as possible, especially for a tech support question , if you have feedback please be civil and try to write it in a constructive manner.  This literally helps me get thru items faster.  


I am super stoked to hear all the feedback and hopefully see some cool creations by you all.  
don't be afraid to ask questions, here or on discord

https://discord.com/invite/falconeer

Cheers,
Tomas Sala

notes.title: A Demo is coming
notes.content:
A demo!
In the new year I want as many gamers to try out Bulwark, so I've decided to start with Base Builder Fest. 
A free demo will  be available during the entire fest. (and probably a bit ahead).

Officially I am declaring this a pre-alpha demo as development is still ongoing. But I've taken time to prepare a voiced tutorial and as much guidance as i can, and I hope players will find a polished experience.

Unlimited
The content in the demo is unlimited , there are no timers or limitations to what you can build, though only 1 starting scenario is unlocked.  You can still fly around the wider Ursee, though it isn't fully developed out yet, but you can build traderoutes and start a colonoy wherever you want. There are some pretty epic spots on the Ursee.  

Tutorial
But it's best to start with the tutorial, which will explain the building system and mechanics such as traderoutes, after the tutorial you can keep building and random encounters will be spawned and captains will sail up to your harbours to offer their services.  

Freebuild
Freebuild mode is also available in the demo, here there are no story elements, no resources , just unlimited building anywhere you want.

[Friends and Enemies]
The demo contains just about all the content I've developed so far for Bulwark, but with quite a bit of development to go it is still pre-alpha and content incomplete..  The main feature that will be added is the ability to make friends and enemies across the Ursee, this more strategical layer isn't available in the demo as it is under development.  

Discord
In general this demo is there for people to get introduced to the freeform building and open world building concept and provide feedback to me so I can improve the game.  If you find bugs or have questions please join the discord and the conversation there :https://discord.com/invite/falconeer


In general have fun and remember this is just a sampling of what's to come.

Cheers,
Tomas Sala

notes.title: Development update
notes.content:
Development update 

So in the previous update I shared about about how NPCs and portraits, I've been working to get the captains part of this functional in the game.  That means when you build a harbor you will get a prompt to pick a captain to sail that future route (once you create a sister harbor they'll get connected and the captain's ship will go back and forth).

Here's a bit of the UI for that,
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42854035/0a6e6f1eaa7cd3c2be837aa9d9819bb65752c0b1.png
I am aiming for a very minimal UX for Bulwark, so information needs to be condensed, in this case you can switch between your inventory of captains and see what kind of effect they'll have on the route. In this case a trade route for steel and workers.  But you can also drop in a combat captain and turn it into a patrol route with a capable warship.

Talking about ships
Every captain will come with their own ship, unique to their task and character.  There will be ships of different factions and of different classes.  Little story events will unlock new captains and move your faction relation in a specific direction and thus later on unlock more capable captains and ships of a friendly faction and fewer of a hostile faction.   

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42854035/d4bdf3a201a619ff0fbe00b2dcddc268e07e41d4.jpg
Here's a look at the Freehouse (civilian) ships including a freehouse clipper, the base warship when you are neutrally aligned.   Players who've played The Falconeer will recognize some of these and notice the extra detail and dynamic trim (that will be a player choice, so there's a bit customisation to the ships and looks of things). 
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42854035/5a9adf67d8c25cf778ab64a4b64300f314e92f9f.jpg
There will be ships and captains to "gather"  from the freehouse, imperial, mancer and possibly pirate and freebooter factions as well, each with their own unique ships (or creatures)..

Factions Overview
just a quick intro for those new to the Falconeer Lore

Freehouse, your average trading and peaceful neutral faction. Civilians,traders and mercenaries basically.
Imperial Remnant, what remains of the great noble houses of the Ursee and their united empire.
Mancer Remnant, the rare remaining bastions of learing and sciece. An order that once controlled all technologies from their massive vaults and thus 'the path' of Ursee civilisations. Now greatly reduced
Pirates, well.... pirates
Freebooter Remnant, a subterranean people with impressive biological tech. Now a scattered tribe forced to wander the Ursee after their homes were destroyed 



That's it for this week, If you have questions or feedback don't be afraid to pop in some comments
Cheerio
Tomas

Hi everyone, 

Tomas here (the Developer of Bulwark), I thought it time to offer  everybody who's following the game a welcome and quick peek on what I'm up to at the moment.  Take note, I'm mostly developing Bulwark alone but getting awesome help from my publisher Wired Productions, Benedict Nichols is onboard to compose and later on I'll get help on porting, QA and help running things.  

For now Its just me plugging away at the game and occasionally some updates from the good people at Wired. I am always around so please comment, post questions, stuff you like, stuff you don't like, it's all good info to me.  

So getting back from Gamescom I was reeling from the announce trailer reception and since then  I've been getting back into the swing of things. The game is playable for shows and such, and some people and press got a demo but it's still early. Still you can already create all the fortresses and towns you saw in the trailer, nothing was faked, all of it just created by plugging away at the current build.   

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42854035/eb1e6e9c11074476d5312ae59c03783134e3355b.png

Captains and Commanders

One thing you've not seen is some of the story bits and NPCs and those will be in the game to spice up your bulwark and make it come alive with little stories and events.  And the idea is that sometimes you'll end up with an NPC (aptly called commanders at this stage) to assign to a tower or a major building, to unlock specific upgrades. One variant of those are captains, these are commanders you assign to a harbor and the associated trade-routes (every harbor is connected to one other harbor to make a trade-route), and they will bring their own ship to sail that trade-route, and if it's a fighting vessel keep it safe. If you've played the Falconeer you might recognize some, though 30 years of war has turned most fleets into collections of make-do and jury rigged vessels of various plumage. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42854035/a57178e484b4c814039ffe223b1b67257050407d.png 

Talking head rendering and design
I've been working on upgrading the NPC system from The Falconeer to visualize the animated portraits for the  NPCs. I use lots of tricks to create content quickly by making elaborate systems first and the NPC generator is one of the more complex systems, for Bulwark I've developed new tools to manually tweak and curate the NPCS instead of full blown procedural, which doesn't always generate the best faces ;). There's also a lot more detail and geometry, even though they retain some of the simple stylings. Remember these will usually be shown reasonably small.
